articles.title: Hasina’s daughter resigns as WHO regional head after fraud allegations
articles.summary: Saima Wazed, the daughter of Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, has resigned from her position as a regional head of the World Health Organization after being placed on unpaid leave following fraud and forgery allegations. Wazed denied the accusations, but the controversy led to her stepping down from the role. The incident has sparked political and public scrutiny in Bangladesh and raised concerns within the WHO about governance and integrity in its regional offices.

articles.title: Nepal cruise into ACC Men’s Premier Cup final
articles.summary: The Nepal cricket team secured a spot in the ACC Men’s Premier Cup final, where they will meet the United Arab Emirates on September 12. The winner of the final will earn a place in the upcoming Asia Cup, marking a significant achievement for Nepalese cricket.

articles.title: Gauri Kumari Yadav resigns as industry minister
articles.summary: Industry Minister Gauri Kumari Yadav has resigned after facing criticism for remarks suggesting that LPG supplies would not improve until the government took action against industrialists. The comments sparked public and political backlash, leading to her departure from the cabinet.

articles.title: How did two controversial religious leaders end up at Gen Z Martyrs’ Day?
articles.summary: Two controversial religious leaders were given prominent speaking slots at the Gen Z Martyrs’ Day memorial programme, prompting criticism from members of the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP). Lawmakers questioned the decision to feature the leaders, citing concerns over their past statements and the potential politicisation of a solemn national observance. The incident has sparked debate over the separation of religion and state, the appropriateness of the event’s lineup, and the broader influence of religious figures in Nepali politics. Officials from the event’s organising committee defended the invitations as an effort to promote inclusivity, while opposition voices demanded a review of the selection process.

articles.title: Climate loss and damage fund moves to consider urgent support for Nepal
articles.summary: The FRLD co-chairs are working with the Board to consider urgent support for Nepal following the August 26 Bhotekoshi floods.

articles.title: Trump touts $5,000 payout if Republicans win as Vance waits in wings
articles.summary: Trump proposes a $5,000 payout if Republicans win, putting him at the centre of the midterm campaign. Vice President JD Vance is set to deliver a keynote that could serve as an early test for his 2028 presidential ambitions.

articles.title: Rapid assessment puts Bhotekoshi recovery needs at Rs723 billion
articles.summary: A rapid assessment estimates that the Bhotekoshi region will need about Rs723 billion for recovery, with roughly three‑quarters of the cost tied to rebuilding infrastructure such as hydropower plants, roads, homes and essential services.

articles.title: Kathmandu Gorkhas continue partnership with Shikhar Insurance
articles.summary: The Kathmandu Gorkhas have renewed their sponsorship agreement with Shikhar Insurance, naming the insurer their 'golden partner' for the upcoming third season of the Nepal Premier League. As part of the deal, Shikhar Insurance's logo will appear on the back of the Gorkhas' jerseys, highlighting the continued collaboration between the cricket team and the insurance firm.

articles.title: Gen Z memorial unveiling put off after families say statues don’t resemble their children
articles.summary: The planned unveiling of a Gen Z memorial in Kathmandu has been postponed after families of the commemorated children complained that the statues do not resemble their loved ones. The families argued that the likenesses are inaccurate and disrespectful, prompting organizers to halt the ceremony. Sculptors involved in the project responded that they were pressured to complete the works quickly and were forced to display unfinished pieces, which they say contributed to the mismatches. The controversy has sparked debate over artistic standards, community consultation, and the handling of public memorial projects in Nepal.

articles.title: A helicopter finally reaches flood-isolated Tiru of Rasuwa, 15 days after the devastating deluge
articles.summary: A helicopter finally reached the flood‑isolated village of Tiru in Rasuwa district, 15 days after the catastrophic floods on August 26 washed away all roads and bridges, cutting off the community from the outside world. The aerial aid marks the first direct relief access since the disaster, bringing essential supplies and hope to the stranded residents.

articles.title: Xi’s India visit to help diplomatic thaw, but business ties bound by suspicion
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping’s recent visit to India is seen as a step toward easing long‑standing diplomatic tensions between the two neighbours. While high‑level talks have opened the door to a modest political thaw, lingering mistrust continues to shape economic interactions. Both governments maintain strict controls on investments, visa processing and the use of Chinese technology, limiting the scope of commercial cooperation. Analysts note that although the diplomatic overture is encouraging, business ties remain constrained by suspicion and regulatory hurdles, suggesting a gradual and cautious normalization of relations.

articles.title: Nepal’s exporters struggle to tap global e-commerce boom
articles.summary: Nepalese exporters are finding it difficult to capitalize on the global surge in e‑commerce due to a combination of high logistics expenses, scarce cross‑border payment solutions, cumbersome regulations, and limited digital infrastructure. These barriers keep local products from reaching major online marketplaces such as Amazon and Alibaba, hampering the country's export growth despite rising worldwide demand for niche and handmade goods. Industry officials and trade bodies are calling for policy reforms, better payment gateways, and investment in digital capabilities to improve competitiveness.

articles.title: Two days of Gen Z uprising, two versions of what happened
articles.summary: The article examines the recent Gen Z protests in Nepal, highlighting the conflicting narratives of the two main sides. The traditional political establishment emphasizes the events of September 9, while the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) government points to a deadly crackdown that occurred on September 8. Both factions have yet to fully investigate or hold anyone accountable for the violence and unrest that unfolded over the two days.

articles.title: At ACC Premier Cup final, it’s the ‘Associate El Clásico’ once again
articles.summary: The ACC Premier Cup final will see Nepal face off against arch‑rival United Arab Emirates after Nepal edged Oman in a low‑scoring semifinal. The match, dubbed the ‘Associate El Clásico’, carries high stakes as the winner secures a direct qualification spot for the 2027 Asia Cup. Both sides are eager to claim the title and the coveted berth, with Nepal looking to build on its recent defensive performance while the UAE aims to overturn past results. The final promises an intense showdown between two of Asia’s leading associate cricket nations.

articles.title: Woman delivers baby on street outside Saptari hospital as couple can’t afford blood test
articles.summary: A woman gave birth on the street outside Gajendra Narayan Singh Hospital in Rajbiraj, Saptari, after she and her husband could not afford a required blood test. The incident highlighted gaps in affordable healthcare, prompting the Health Ministry and the Nepal Medical Council to send investigative teams to the hospital.

articles.title: Consumers struggle with declining LPG import, transport disruption
articles.summary: Residents of Kathmandu are enduring long queues for cooking gas as a combination of reduced LPG imports, highway blockages and distribution bottlenecks has tightened supply. The shortage has driven up prices and sparked public frustration, culminating in the resignation of Nepal's commerce minister. Authorities cite pent‑up demand and transport disruptions as the main causes, while consumers worry about future availability and affordability of LPG.

articles.title: How the melting glaciers are unlocking ancient superbugs we’ve never seen before
articles.summary: Researchers warn that as Himalayan glaciers melt, long‑dormant pathogens and ancient antibiotic‑resistance genes are being released into freshwater systems, creating a new public‑health threat. The study highlights how climate‑induced glacier loss could unlock previously unseen superbugs, potentially spreading disease and undermining modern antibiotics.

articles.title: Lessons from Nepal’s past for families living without answers
articles.summary: The article reflects on the lingering trauma faced by families still searching for answers after the devastating flood in Nepal. While physical reconstruction may be ongoing, the emotional and psychological wounds persist, leaving many without closure. The author urges a collaborative approach, emphasizing that walking alongside survivors—providing both material aid and compassionate support—can help families navigate the uncertainty and begin healing. By learning from past experiences, communities can better address the long‑term needs of those affected.

articles.title: Nepalis are still struggling to find cooking gas. The government cannot afford to ignore it
articles.summary: Many Nepali households continue to face shortages of cooking gas, prompting criticism of the government's response. The article urges authorities to clearly communicate and guarantee reliable access to LPG, highlighting the impact on daily life and calling for policy action.

articles.title: What if your ‘bad posture’ is actually not that bad?
articles.summary: The article challenges the long‑standing advice to maintain a rigid, upright posture, suggesting that there is no single ‘correct’ way to sit. Instead, it emphasizes the importance of regular movement and avoiding prolonged static positions to reduce discomfort and potential health issues. The piece encourages readers to focus on dynamic posture habits rather than strict alignment.

articles.title: Houthis advance along Yemeni coast, threaten Saudi oil exports in the Red Sea
articles.summary: The Houthi rebels have seized control of the Yemeni port city of Mocha and are advancing toward the strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait. Their movements heighten fears that Red Sea shipping lanes could be disrupted, threatening Saudi Arabia's oil export routes. The escalation comes amid heightened US‑Iran tensions, further complicating regional energy security. Analysts warn that any blockage of the Bab el‑Mandeb could have global repercussions for oil markets and maritime trade.

articles.title: One found dead inside burned-out vehicle in Bharatpur
articles.summary: Police discovered a dead person inside a vehicle that had caught fire on the service lane of the East‑West Highway near Bharatpur. The vehicle was found burned out, and authorities are investigating the circumstances of the fire and the fatality.

articles.title: For people with disabilities, surviving Nepal’s floods was only the beginning
articles.summary: The article discusses the challenges faced by people with disabilities in Nepal after floods, including finding safe routes and accessing shelters.

articles.title: Rybakina beats Gauff to book US Open final against Sabalenka
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina rallied after dropping the first set to defeat Coco Gauff and secure her first US Open final appearance. The Kazakhstani star will meet defending champion Aryna Sabalenka in the championship match, setting up a high‑profile showdown at the tournament's climax.

articles.title: Landslide dams Solukhumbu river, spurring downstream flood warnings
articles.summary: A recent landslide has created a temporary dam on the Solukhumbu River near Hunga Khola, causing water to spill over the blockage. Authorities have warned that the dam is unstable and could burst, posing a flood risk to downstream villages. Residents have been urged to stay clear of the riverbanks while officials monitor the situation and prepare evacuation plans. The incident highlights ongoing concerns about landslide hazards in Nepal's mountainous regions.
